findings.finding: Arkema beat its own compiled EBITDA consensus in both 2026 quarters so far: Q1 EUR282.7m vs EUR267m (+6%) and Q2 EUR390.9m vs EUR362m (+8%). The Q3 consensus of EUR328m implies +5.8% YoY against Q2's +7.4%, and a Q3/Q2 ratio of 0.84, at the bottom of the 2024-25 seasonal range (0.85 in 2025).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose on each of the last four results days: Q3'25 +4.75% (2025-11-07), FY25 +1.99% (2026-02-26), Q1'26 +2.56% (2026-05-06, an EBITDA beat), Q2'26 +5.25% (2026-07-30, the +8% beat). Beats have been bought here, not sold.
findings.original_quote: EBITDA de 390,9 M EUR contre 362 M EUR attendus par le consensus fourni par la société (Q2); Q1: 282,7 M EUR contre un consensus de 267 millions d'euros attendus par le consensus fourni par l'entreprise -- translation: Q2 EBITDA EUR390.9m against EUR362m expected by the company-provided consensus; Q1 EUR282.7m against EUR267m
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 consensus range is tight (320-338) and its midpoint grows more slowly than Q2 did, so sell-side has not extrapolated the two beats. If the pattern were priced, the consensus would sit nearer EUR345-350m, or the stock would have recovered the post-Q2 level (EUR62.10 on 30 July). It is EUR57.65 and -7.5% over 60 days despite a +5% 20-day bounce.

findings.finding: Peers that have already reported Q3 2026 show strong price pass-through in European and US chemicals. BASF's Q3 EBITDA bSI rose ~15% on prices +12%, with every core segment up, and it narrowed its FY range upward to EUR7.4-7.8bn. Dow's Industrial Intermediates showed local price +16% and an EBIT swing from -$47m to +$176m. H.B. Fuller (adhesives, quarter to August) had adj. EBITDA +9% on pricing +7.4%. Wacker's Q3 earnings rose. Against that, AkzoNobel (coatings) had flat revenue on volume -2%, though its margin expanded.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Arkema closed flat (55.20 -> 55.20) on BASF's 2026-10-28 print, so the read-across was not traded on that day. The stock is +4.4% over the five sessions into the print, which partly prices it.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission: Arkema's own consensus (EUR328m, +5.8% YoY) grows at well under half BASF's rate. Arkema's mix (acrylics in Primary Materials, Bostik adhesives, coating resins) overlaps BASF Chemicals and H.B. Fuller directly. Had the market priced the read-across, the consensus range would not top out at EUR338m. The 5-day run-up shows part of it is in, hence the small size.

findings.finding: The FY26 guide ('EBITDA slightly higher than last year', about EUR1.25bn in 2025) comes after an H1 of EUR673.5m (-2.7%), so it needs H2 of about EUR590-600m, roughly +7% on H2 2025's ~EUR559m. Consensus (EUR1,271m) already sits on it, management warned that the Middle East situation 'ne s'est pas encore stabilisée', and Evonik guided for Q4 normalisation if supply chains stabilise. So the Q3 release's Q4 commentary is the main downside risk to the guide line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance was confirmed at Q1 and Q2 2026 and the stock rose both days. At Q3 2025 the FY guide was set at the low end (~EUR1.25bn) and the stock still rose 4.75%, off a depressed base.
findings.original_quote: Arkema est confiant de pouvoir réaliser sa guidance d'un EBITDA 2026 légèrement supérieur à l'an dernier à taux de change constants ... Au second semestre, nous resterons vigilants vis-à-vis de la situation au Moyen-Orient, qui ne s'est pas encore stabilisée. -- translation: Arkema is confident of delivering its guidance of 2026 EBITDA slightly above last year at constant FX ... In the second half we will remain vigilant regarding the Middle East situation, which has not yet stabilised.
findings.why_not_priced: The wording is qualitative, so the market has no number for how Q4 is guided. Consensus at EUR1,271m on the guide means a narrowed guide at 'around EUR1.25-1.26bn' would be a cut relative to the street. Nobody can price that until the wording is replaced by a number.
